checks.name: Port with no country
checks.detection: country IS NULL
checks.recommendation: Fix: fill from the PORT_FIXES lookup (BEANR is Antwerp, Belgium). One known port, the value is certain, and country is a reporting attribute.

checks.name: Duplicate port code
checks.detection: port_code appears on more than one row
checks.recommendation: Drop: ports is the join target for every other file, so the key must be unique.

checks.name: Congestion score outside 0-1
checks.detection: avg_congestion_score does not parse as a number, or is not between 0 and 1
checks.recommendation: Flag: the score is documented as 0-1, but the correct value is unknowable, so keep the row and exclude the score from features until it is confirmed.

checks.name: Exact duplicate row
checks.detection: surplus rows: count minus count distinct over all columns
checks.recommendation: Drop: byte-identical copies add no information and would double-count the booking.

checks.name: Same shipment_id, different values
checks.detection: shipment_id appears on more than one distinct row
checks.recommendation: Fix: keep one row per id (most complete, then first in file order). The copies differ only in cargo_type or weight_tons, and no source says which is right.

checks.name: Missing required field
checks.detection: shipment_id, origin/destination port or a planned/booking date is NULL
checks.recommendation: Quarantine: a booking without a key, route or schedule cannot be joined, served or labelled, and nothing can be inferred for the blank.

checks.name: Unparseable timestamp or number
checks.detection: a required timestamp, container_count or weight does not parse in its format
checks.recommendation: Quarantine: guessing a date format (2024/06/23 could be day-first) risks silently wrong dates; keep the raw row for manual repair.

checks.name: shipment_id not SHP-NNNNN
checks.detection: shipment_id does not match ^SHP-\d{5}$
checks.recommendation: Flag: the id may still be unique and usable, but it is outside the documented key format, so surface it rather than rewrite a business key.

checks.name: Origin port not in ports
checks.detection: origin_port NOT IN (SELECT port_code FROM ports)
checks.recommendation: Quarantine: placeholder codes (XXTST, ZZZZZ, UNKNW) have no real port behind them, so route features and the port join are impossible.

checks.name: Destination port not in ports
checks.detection: destination_port NOT IN (SELECT port_code FROM ports)
checks.recommendation: Quarantine: same reasoning as the origin port; the destination cannot be recovered.

checks.name: Origin equals destination
checks.detection: origin_port = destination_port
checks.recommendation: Quarantine: a container shipment cannot start and end at the same port, so one of the two fields is wrong and neither can be trusted.

checks.name: Status spelling variant
checks.detection: status not canonical but its upper-case form is a known status or alias
checks.recommendation: Fix: map COMPLETED/Complete/delivered to DELIVERED via STATUS_MAP; same meaning, different spelling.

checks.name: Status missing or N/A
checks.detection: status IS NULL or status = 'N/A'
checks.recommendation: Fix: set to NULL (unknown) and keep the row; do not guess a status. Excluded from status-based analysis, still usable where the label comes from the dates.

checks.name: Cargo type case/whitespace variant
checks.detection: cargo_type not canonical but trim/lower matches a canonical value
checks.recommendation: Fix: trim and map to the canonical casing; the match is unambiguous.

checks.name: Cargo type missing
checks.detection: cargo_type IS NULL
checks.recommendation: Flag: keep the row with cargo_type NULL rather than impute; cargo type cannot be derived from other columns.

checks.name: Weight missing
checks.detection: weight_tons IS NULL
checks.recommendation: Flag: keep NULL and let the model handle missing values; imputing a weight would invent data.

checks.name: Negative weight
checks.detection: weight_tons cast to DOUBLE < 0
checks.recommendation: Fix: set to NULL; a negative weight is impossible and the sign flip is not provably the only error.

checks.name: Zero weight
checks.detection: weight_tons cast to DOUBLE = 0
checks.recommendation: Fix: set to NULL and flag; a loaded container weighs something, and zero is a placeholder, not a measurement.

checks.name: Container count is zero
checks.detection: container_count cast to INTEGER = 0 (valid range starts at 1)
checks.recommendation: Fix: set to NULL and flag. A booking has at least one container, so the count is wrong, but the true value is unknown; the row stays, the count stays out of features.

checks.name: Container count implausible (negative or very high)
checks.detection: container_count cast to INTEGER < 0 or > 100 (zero has its own check)
checks.recommendation: Fix: set to NULL and flag. The bulk is 1-60 and the outliers (510-996) look like entry errors with no way to correct them; a cap would be a guess.

checks.name: Planned arrival before planned departure
checks.detection: planned_arrival < planned_departure
checks.recommendation: Quarantine: an impossible schedule makes planned transit time negative, and the delay label is measured against planned arrival.

checks.name: Planned departure before booking
checks.detection: planned_departure < booking_date
checks.recommendation: Flag: a departure planned before the booking exists is odd but does not break the label; keep the row and watch the count.

checks.name: Actual departure before booking
checks.detection: actual_departure < booking_date
checks.recommendation: Fix: set actual_departure to NULL and flag. The timeline is impossible, but the arrival is plausible, so the row and its delay label are kept.

checks.name: Actual arrival before actual departure
checks.detection: actual_arrival < actual_departure
checks.recommendation: Flag: an impossible transit; the label uses actual_arrival, so treat the row's label as suspect.

checks.name: Completed status but no actual arrival
checks.detection: a status that maps to DELIVERED (upper(status) IN ('COMPLETE', 'COMPLETED', 'DELIVERED')) with actual_arrival IS NULL — the same predicate the pipeline flags
checks.recommendation: Flag: the status claims delivery but there is no arrival to label from. Keep the row unlabelled instead of trusting either field.

checks.name: Status contradicts measured delay
checks.detection: DELIVERED with delay > 24h, or DELAYED with delay <= 24h (actual_arrival - planned_arrival)
checks.recommendation: Flag: status is a leaky copy of the label, so it must not be a feature; where the two disagree, trust the timestamps.

checks.name: event_id reused for different events
checks.detection: event_id appears on more than one distinct row
checks.recommendation: Flag: nothing joins on event_id, so keep every distinct event and key on the row rather than the id.

checks.name: Exact duplicate event
checks.detection: surplus rows: count minus count distinct over all columns
checks.recommendation: Drop: identical copies double-count the event in port-level aggregates.

checks.name: Event port not in ports
checks.detection: port_code NOT IN (SELECT port_code FROM ports)
checks.recommendation: Flag: the event cannot be joined to a port, so it is kept for the event log but excluded from any per-port aggregate (no FK is enforced on port_events).

checks.name: Unparseable or negative event value
checks.detection: event_timestamp does not parse, or delay_minutes is not an INTEGER or is negative
checks.recommendation: Fix: a negative or unparseable delay becomes NULL and the event is kept; an unparseable timestamp cannot be fixed and would surface here before ingestion.

checks.name: Event type missing
checks.detection: event_type IS NULL
checks.recommendation: Flag: keep the event with event_type NULL; delay_minutes is still valid for port delay aggregates.

checks.name: Event type not recognised
checks.detection: event_type is not NULL and not in EVENT_TYPES
checks.recommendation: Fix: set to NULL alongside the blanks (flagged event_type_unknown) rather than guess.

checks.name: Placeholder vessel id
checks.detection: vessel_id IN ('VSL-0000', 'VSL-9999')
checks.recommendation: Fix: set vessel_id to NULL; the event is real port activity, only the vessel is unknown, and the feed is used at port level.

checks.name: Notes missing
checks.detection: notes IS NULL
checks.recommendation: None: notes are free text, nullable by design, and are not used by any feature.

checks.name: 'Normal operations' with a delay
checks.detection: notes = 'Normal operations' and delay_minutes > 0
checks.recommendation: None: the 0-60 minute delays are in the normal range for any event type and the note is a canned label; delay_minutes is the measurement, so trust it over the note.

checks.name: DELAYED event with zero delay
checks.detection: event_type = 'DELAYED' and delay_minutes = 0
checks.recommendation: Flag: a handful of rows; the type and the measurement disagree, so keep the row and use delay_minutes as measured.

checks.name: Timestamp earlier than previous row
checks.detection: event_timestamp < the previous row's (file order)
checks.recommendation: Flag: the feed should arrive sorted; consumers must sort by timestamp rather than rely on file order.
